title: Reading the Tea Leaves, Again: Can Large Language Models Predict Language Model Training Runs?
abstract: arXiv:2611.30141v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM agents now propose research ideas and run the experiments that test them, but they train every run to its end, whereas a researcher reads a run's configuration and the beginning of its curve and stops the runs that show no promise. Reading a run this way takes more than describing or implementing a training method: it takes knowing what a design choice does to a run. We build Tea Leaves to measure this knowledge on 682 real training runs across pretraining, fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning (RL): a forecaster sees the first 20% of a run with its configuration, description, and code, and predicts the rest. Across 11 LLMs and a range of forecasting baselines, the strongest LLMs match or exceed the best curve fitter on smooth loss curves (skill 0.66 against 0.62) and lead on noisy RL reward curves (0.43 against 0.13). translated_title: 再度解读茶渣征兆：大语言模型能否预测语言模型的训练运行？
translated_abstract: 如今，LLM智能体已能够提出研究想法并运行验证这些想法的实验，但它们会将每一次训练运行都执行到底；而人类研究者则会通过阅读训练运行的配置和曲线的开端，停止那些没有前景的运行。以这种方式解读一次训练运行，需要的不仅仅是描述或实现某个训练方法，而是要了解一个设计选择会对训练运行产生何种影响。我们构建了Tea Leaves来衡量这种知识，涵盖预训练、微调和强化学习（RL）共682个真实训练运行：预测者可以看到一次训练运行的前20%，包括其配置、描述和代码，并据此预测其余部分。在11个LLM和一系列预测基线方法的对比中，最强的LLM在平滑的损失曲线上达到甚至超过了最佳曲线拟合器的水平（技能分数0.66对0.62），并在有噪声的RL奖励曲线上明显领先（0.43对0.13）。限制所有预测者的关键在于日志所承载的信息：在日志记录稀疏的社区运行数据上，所有方法都损失了大部分……
tldr: 该论文提出了Tea Leaves基准，通过让大语言模型根据训练运行前20%的配置、描述、代码和曲线来预测其余结果，在682个真实训练运行上评估了11个LLM的预测能力，发现最强LLM在平滑损失曲线上可比肩最佳曲线拟合器，而在有噪声的强化学习奖励曲线上则显著领先。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Tea Leaves, a benchmark that measures whether LLMs can predict the outcomes of language model training runs from the first 20% of each run's configuration, description, code, and curve across 682 real runs, finding that the strongest LLMs match or exceed the best curve fitter on smooth loss curves and substantially lead on noisy RL reward curves.
